newsitem.title: USA: Voters oppose Seattle football stadium plan - poll.
newsitem.headline: Voters oppose Seattle football stadium plan - poll.

text.p: Billionaire Paul Allen's plan to build a $425 million football stadium using taxpayer funding appears to be in trouble, according to a poll published Wednesday.

A survey of 800 likely voters in the June 17 statewide single-question election found 56 percent opposed to the idea of a new tax-supported professional football stadium in Seattle and only 38 percent in favour.

The poll, published in the Seattle Post-Intelligencer, was taken last week before a court ruling slightly changed the ballot language to reflect the possibility the stadium also could be used for soccer.

Allen, co-founder of Microsoft Corp. and one of the richest men in the country, has insisted on a statewide vote approving taxpayer funding for the planned new stadium before he will exercise his option to buy the Seattle Seahawks. The option expires July 1.

Last month the Washington Legislature approved a $329 million funding package for the stadium to replace the 21-year-old Kingdome. Money will be raised from a new lottery game, an extension of King County's hotel tax, existing sales tax and parking and ticket taxes.

Before Allen took the option to buy the National Football League team, owner Ken Behring was trying to move it to California, and most of those surveyed believe the team will be moved if the stadium package fails.
Of those surveyed, 70 percent agreed professional football was an important asset to the region, but 68 percent said they thought Allen could afford to build the stadium himself.
The poll was conducted for the newspaper and KOMO-TV by GMA Research and had a margin of error of 3.5 percent, the newspaper said.
